title: UK retail sales rise 0.7% in October, beating forecasts
story: British retail sales volumes unexpectedly rose 0.7% in October compared with September, official
show today. Economists polled by Reuters had a median
that sales volumes would be unchanged on the month. UK consumer sentiment had fallen sharply in October, according to Britain's longest-running measure of this, as rising fuel bills and borrowing
squeezed households, although November data showed ⁠a small recovery. Consumer price

rose to a one-year high of 3.6% in October and the Bank of England forecast it would reach close to 5% in the middle of next ‌year when it raised interest rates for the first time in three years ⁠this month. However, overall economic
has ‌been stronger than expected this year and recent updates from ⁠major ‌British retailers have been mixed.
